summary: A recursive common table expression starts with anchor rows and repeatedly derives new rows from earlier results.
syntax: WITH RECURSIVE sequence AS (anchor UNION ALL recursive_step) SELECT ...
documentation: A recursive common table expression starts with anchor rows and repeatedly derives new rows from earlier results. A terminating condition bounds the recursion. The final SELECT determines display order.
inputs: An anchor query, recursive query and stopping condition.
returns: Rows generated by the final query.
caution: An incorrect stopping rule can create excessive work. Keep generated ranges bounded and do not rely on implicit result ordering.
scenarios: Generate a short sequence of reporting offsets.
Expand a bounded parent-child hierarchy for a report.
Create numbered planning slots without storing a permanent sequence table.
title: Generate reporting offsets
problem: Table settings(max_day INTEGER) contains exactly one row with max_day from 0 through 20. Return one column day containing every integer from 0 through max_day inclusive, ordered ascending.
goal: Use WITH RECURSIVE or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Anchor at zero and recurse while day is below the configured maximum.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query against the supplied tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Several offsets
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE settings(max_day INTEGER);INSERT INTO settings VALUES(3);

tests.name: Zero bound
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE settings(max_day INTEGER);INSERT INTO settings VALUES(0);

tests.name: One step
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE settings(max_day INTEGER);INSERT INTO settings VALUES(1);
